key_insight: Oxygen content in submerged arc welding controls surface-tension-driven flow reversal in the molten pool, shifting the balance from wide outward spreading to narrower inward-return circulation and deeper penetration.
engineering_relevance: By regulating flux oxygen supply, welders can tune bead width, penetration depth, and rear solidification behavior to improve weld formation control.
method: Developed a numerical framework coupling multi-pathway oxygen transport with dynamic, region-specific surface tension.
Simulated molten-pool flow across varying oxygen levels to track Marangoni convection and vortex formation.
Compared spreading vs. centripetal flow dominance to explain changes in pool shape and solidification behavior.
evidence_signal: Simulation results across oxygen levels showed flow-pattern transitions, pool-width contraction at higher oxygen, and deeper penetration with delayed rear solidification.
watch_item: The framework is simulation-based, so practical transferability depends on how well flux oxygen transport and surface-tension parameters match real welding conditions.
paper_title: Influence of Oxygen Content upon Molten Pool Dynamics in Submerged Arc Welding
